It uses a `DataUpdateCoordinator` to fetch project tasks rather than issuing a separate network request for each project the user has configured.

Logger: urllib3.connectionpool

First occurred: 2:38:06 PM (214 occurrences)

Connection pool is full, discarding connection: api.todoist.com. Connection pool size: 10
Same here. Is this problem rooted in the Todoist integration for home assistant or directly at Todoist (API)? Maybe @boralyl can help?

Looked into this briefly.  Before the integration broke it was using the sync-api.  Essentially it made a single request and retrieved all project and task data.

The rest-api works differently and data must be requested separately in some instances.  I do see some areas for improvement to reduce the connections and get rid of the warnings:

1. There isn't an api endpoint to fetch all collaborators. So when the component is setup it issues a request to get collaborators for every project. So if you had 10 projects we'd fire off 10 requests right off the bat.  This appears to only be used so that you can specify an assignee when using the create task service. I'm not sure if anyone uses this feature or not.  I believe this could be fixed by simply fetching collaborators at the time of calling the create new task service.
2. When fetching events for the calendar or updating one of the calendar entities we issue 1 request per project.  This could be improved to use a [DataUpdateCoordinator](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/integration_fetching_data/#coordinated-single-api-poll-for-data-for-all-entities) to make a single request to get all tasks rather than 1 request per project.

I believe addressing those 2 tasks should resolve the warnings in the logs.  Both of these would be separate tasks to keep PR's focused so I wouldn't expect fixing only 1 of the above to resolve the warnings.

Still getting this error on HA 2023.3.0.

@boralyl - any thoughts on if/when this can be fixed? Thanks :)
Not sure if this is part of the same problem, but in my AdGuard DNS logs I'm getting dozens of requests to api.todoist.com every second originating from Home Assistant.

I've got 2 PRs that I can verify correct this issue.  If anyone on this issue has the time or ability to do some reviews the PRs can be found here:

* https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/87957
* https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/89836

After both of these are merged the issue will be resolved.
FYI even though this was auto-closed it's not yet fixed unil the last PR is merged which should happen soon. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/89836

review_comments:
This change to use a coordinator generally makes sense. One thing I would like to point out is that the `TodoistProjectData` class is effectively trying to act partially like a data update coordinator. In Google Calendar, which this copied from, I was able to remove this once moving to a coordinator, since it isn't offering much value once you unwind it.

The other thing to consider is that the coordinator is still polling once per minute if I understand correctly. I assume that is more that is needed from a todo list cloud api, but it does mean you get faster updates when things change. The strategy taken by google calendar has always been to have it poll the cloud every 15 minutes, then have the entity itself update every minute so it still advances the clock. (requires a bit of entity adjustment to allow polling at a different interval)

That sounds reasonable, I'm not sure what the original intent is for the 1 minute interval was it seems a bit much.  I'll make a note to look into this in the future.  Getting rid of the other class would be great too.
The 1 minute interval is likely there just to make sure events start on time. Once you separate the two objects like you have here, now you can tweak the two intervals separately.
I wasn't 100% sure how to verify a failed update, but this appears to simulate what would happen if an update on setup failed.  If you have suggestions or examples that might be better let me know.

I updated this based on a comment in the [DataUpdateCoordinator](https://github.com/boralyl/home-assistant/blob/48fca3bb2727b393d29f2246bc4df98ba8c35ed6/homeassistant/helpers/update_coordinator.py#L76-L80) from the previous `coordinator.async_refresh()`.
